issues.legal_issue: A recurring allowance granted in consideration of relinquishing rights in land and land revenue, but not itself constituting an interest in land or land revenue, is not extinguished merely because the land estates vest in the State.
material_facts: The allowance arose from a compromise of a civil dispute over the resumption of rights in land and was granted in consideration of relinquishing those rights.

The allowance relating to the settled villages was calculated as a share of net revenue, but the Government collected the entire land revenue and the recipients had no interest or obligation in its collection.
The allowance was described as a pension and was paid annually; its amount was measured by reference to revenue rather than being a right to that revenue.

The recipient's right to the allowance was not an estate or an assignment of land revenue recorded in the relevant revenue records, and the statutory compensation scheme did not provide compensation for that allowance.
The dispute concerned the effect of statutory vesting of land estates on a pre-existing allowance.
issues.conclusion: The allowance granted in consideration for relinquishing rights in the settled villages was not extinguished by the vesting of the estates, and the order requiring its continued payment was confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4 and 6(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, vesting extinguishes estates and rights or privileges directly connected with land in an estate or its land revenue. An allowance granted as consideration for extinguishing a former right to land or land revenue is distinct from such a right, even when its amount is measured by reference to revenue. Sections 37–45 provide for compensation to specified intermediaries; section 45 is a machinery provision and does not enlarge the rights extinguished under section 6. A person receiving this kind of allowance is not, by that fact alone, an assignee of land revenue for purposes of section 32(a)–(d) of the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

issues.definition: When a vesting dispute concerns an allowance granted for relinquishing land rights, and the allowance is only measured by revenue rather than being an interest in that land or revenue, the allowance right survives vesting if it is not recorded as a land-revenue assignment.

issues.legal_issue: A right to remission of land revenue in an estate ends when the recipient's proprietary right in that estate vests in the State and cannot be converted into a right to receive the remitted amount.
material_facts: The recipient was a proprietor of twelve mahals that constituted an estate.
The arrangement granted a remission of part of the land revenue assessed on those mahals, rather than a separate pension payable from the revenue collected on other villages.
The recipient's proprietary right in the twelve mahals vested in the State under the statutory notification.
The recipient sought to claim the amount of the remission as a positive payment after the proprietary right in the mahals had ceased.
issues.conclusion: The right to remission in respect of the twelve mahals ended upon vesting, and the recipient was not entitled to receive the remitted amount as a payment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(8) and 4 of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, provide for an estate and the vesting of rights in it in the State. Under section 6(b), grants or confirmations of rights or privileges in respect of land in an acquired estate or its land revenue determine. A remission of land revenue is a right directly in respect of revenue from the estate; once the recipient's interest in that estate ceases, the remission cannot be transformed into a positive payment. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.
